prs.title: Enforce `max_file_size` for `/component_server` multipart uploads
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #13556.

`launch(max_file_size=...)` was enforced for `/upload` but **bypassed** by multipart requests to `/component_server`. The multipart branch parsed the request with Starlette's `request.form()` and called `await value.read()` on each uploaded file, materializing the full contents into memory before dispatching to the component function — so an app launched with a small `max_file_size` could still be forced to read arbitrarily large files.

## Root cause & fix

The `/component_server` multipart branch in `gradio/routes.py` used `request.form()` (no size enforcement). This PR parses the body with `GradioMultiPartParser` using `blocks.max_file_size` — the same path `/upload` uses — so oversized uploads are rejected with **413** during streaming, before the whole file is read into memory. The parser's temporary files are cleaned up after their contents are read.

## Verification

Minimal repro (from the issue), run against the branch — `/component_server` now matches `/upload`:

```python
import gradio as gr
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    file_explorer = gr.FileExplorer(root_dir=".")

app, _, _ = demo.launch(prevent_thread_lock=True, max_file_size="1kb", _frontend=False)
try:
    client = TestClient(app)
    large = b"x" * 2048
    print("upload   ", client.post("/gradio_api/upload",
        files={"files": ("big.bin", large, "application/octet-stream")}).status_code)
    print("component", client.post("/gradio_api/component_server/",
        data={"session_hash": "123", "component_id": str(file_explorer._id), "fn_name": "ls"},
        files={"payload": ("big.bin", large, "application/octet-stream")}).status_code)
finally:
    demo.close()
```

- **Before:** `upload 413`; `component` parsed the file and dispatched to `FileExplorer.ls` (`TypeError: object of type 'DataWithFiles' has no len()`) instead of rejecting it.
- **After:** `upload 413`; `component 413` (`File size exceeded maximum allowed size of 1024 bytes.`).

Added regression test `test_max_file_size_used_in_component_server_route` in `test/test_routes.py` (posts a >1 KiB multipart body to `/component_server/` and asserts 413; a sub-limit file is not rejected for size). Verified it **fails on `main`** (`assert 500 == 413`) and **passes** with this fix.

```bash
python -m pytest test/test_routes.py -k "upload or component or multipart or file or blob"
# 20 passed
```

The demo file was not committed.

prs.title: Make client `predict()` reject on unknown endpoint so errors are catchable
prs.body:
Fixes #12101. Good for `gr.Server` apps.

When the JS client's `Client.predict()` is called with an endpoint name (or `fn_index`) that doesn't exist, the resulting `"There is no endpoint matching that name of fn_index matching that number."` error was **not catchable** — neither `try/catch` nor `.catch()` on the returned promise could handle it, and it surfaced as an `unhandledRejection` that crashes the calling process.

## Root cause

`predict()` runs its body inside `new Promise(async (resolve, reject) => { ... })` (the async Promise-executor anti-pattern). `submit()` throws **synchronously** via `get_endpoint_info` when the endpoint can't be resolved. Because the executor is an `async` function with no `try/catch`, that throw rejects the executor's *own discarded* promise rather than the promise `predict()` returns. The returned promise therefore never settles, so `await`/`.catch()` never see the error and it escapes as an unhandled rejection.

## Fix

Wrap the executor body in `try/catch` and call `reject(error)`, so a synchronous throw from `submit()` (or any error during iteration) rejects the promise `predict()` returns.

## Verification

Repro against a local Gradio app with one named endpoint, calling `predict()` on a nonexistent endpoint:

- **Before:** `.catch()`/`try` did not fire; error escaped as `unhandledRejection`; the awaited promise never settled.
- **After:** `.catch()` fires with the error; no `unhandledRejection`.

Added a regression test in `client/js/src/test/submit.test.ts` (`predict error handling`) that asserts `predict()` rejects (rather than hanging/throwing uncatchably) for an unknown endpoint. Verified it **fails** on `main` ("predict() never settled") and **passes** with this fix.

```bash
cd client/js && NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 TEST_MODE=node pnpm exec vitest run -c vite.config.ts src/test/submit.test.ts
# 4 passed
```

Minimal server used for manual verification (not committed):

```python
import gradio as gr

def greet(name):
    return f"Hello {name}"

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    inp = gr.Textbox()
    out = gr.Textbox()
    inp.submit(greet, inp, out, api_name="greet")

demo.launch(server_port=7810)
```

```js
// nonexistent endpoint -> now catchable
const app = await Client.connect("http://127.0.0.1:7810");
await app.predict("nonexistent_endpoint", { name: "x" }).catch((e) => {
  console.log("caught:", e.message); // fires now
});
```

prs.title: Fix `gr.ImageEditor` high CPU usage when idle
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #7586

`gr.ImageEditor` pinned the CPU (70%+ in the reporter's case) whenever its browser tab was focused, even when the editor was completely idle.

### Root cause

The ImageEditor is built on Pixi.js, whose `Application` ticker auto-renders the stage every animation frame (`autoStart` defaults to `true`). On top of that, the editor adds a per-frame ticker callback that clears and redraws the canvas outline/overlay graphics. Nothing ever gates this, so the editor fully re-rendered at the display's refresh rate (60–120+ fps) forever — even when nothing on screen was changing. This matches the diagnosis from @pngwn on the issue ("the internal ticker that handles frame redraws runs always").

### Fix

Make the render loop idle-aware (`js/imageeditor/shared/core/editor.ts`). The ticker now stops itself after 500 ms of no activity, and is woken again on any signal that can change the scene:

- **Pointer/wheel events over the canvas** — brush drawing, the brush cursor following the pointer, crop-handle dragging, panning.
- **Spring animation frames** — zoom, pan, resize and image-fitting all animate through the `scale`/`position`/`dimensions` springs.
- **Discrete mutations** — `notify` (change/input), tool/subtool switches, layer add/remove/reorder/visibility, canvas resize and reset.

While idle the ticker is fully stopped, so the editor uses no CPU/GPU until the next interaction. The frame that crosses the idle threshold is still rendered (the renderer runs at a lower ticker priority later in the same tick), so the final state is always flushed and there is no stale-canvas flicker.

All existing rendering behaviour during interactions/animations is unchanged — the loop simply sleeps when there is nothing to draw.

### Verification

Built the frontend and ran a Playwright probe that counts frames actually rendered by the editor's ticker (`window.editor.app.ticker`):

```
Idle (2s, no interaction):      0 frames   | ticker.started=false
Interacting (2s, drawing):      221 frames | ticker.started=true
Idle again (2s):                0 frames   | ticker.started=false
```

So the editor renders ~110 fps while you draw and drops to a completely stopped ticker (0 frames) when idle. Before this change the ticker never stopped.

Existing ImageEditor e2e specs pass, confirming drawing, erasing, cropping, change/input events, uploads, clearing and canvas resizing still work:
- `image_editor_events` — 7/7 passed
- `image_editor_canvas_size` — passed

### Minimal repro demo (not committed)

```python
import gradio as gr


def edit_image(im):
    return [im["background"].size, im["background"], im["layers"][0], im["composite"]]


with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    with gr.Tab("ImageEditor"):
        im = gr.ImageEditor(type="pil")
        with gr.Group():
            with gr.Row():
                text_out = gr.Textbox(label="Edited Size")
            with gr.Row():
                im_out_1 = gr.Image(type="pil", label="Background")
                im_out_2 = gr.Image(type="pil", label="Layer 0")
                im_out_3 = gr.Image(type="pil", label="Composite")
        im.change(edit_image, outputs=[text_out, im_out_1, im_out_2, im_out_3], inputs=im)

demo.launch()
```

Open the ImageEditor, leave it idle, and watch the tab's CPU usage: it now drops to ~0 instead of staying pinned.

prs.title: Remove unused external deps (bokeh/plotly/opencv) from e2e test setup
prs.body:
Follow up from https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/pull/13568, closes #11310.

I'll merge this in too when green since it's just CI

## Root cause

The `functional` workflow ran an **install dependencies for specific tests** step before the browser tests:

```yaml
uv pip install -r demo/outbreak_forecast/requirements.txt   # numpy, matplotlib, bokeh, plotly, altair
uv pip install -r demo/stream_video_out/requirements.txt    # opencv-python
```

Of those packages, the only ones **not already in `test/requirements.txt`** (installed for all functional CI) are **bokeh, plotly, and opencv-python**. And those three are used *only* by the two demos above — both of whose e2e specs are **entirely skipped**:

- `js/spa/test/outbreak_forecast.spec.ts` — every test is `test.fixme(...)`
- `js/spa/test/stream_video_out.spec.ts` — every test is `test.skip(...)` ("Not supported in CI")

Because the skips are at the declaration level, Playwright never runs their (auto) fixtures, so the demo apps are never launched and the external deps are never imported. The install step was pure overhead — uncached, slow, and an extra failure point on an already-flaky path (exactly as the issue describes).

## Fix

- Remove the `install dependencies for specific tests` step from `.github/workflows/test-functional.yml`.
- Remove the matching `pip install -r demo/.../requirements.txt` lines from the contributor docs (`js/README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`) — which also addresses the stale setup steps noted in #11309.

No change to which tests actually run. Every other e2e demo only needs packages already present in `test/requirements.txt` (numpy, pandas, pillow, matplotlib, altair) — verified by cross-referencing each spec's demo `requirements.txt` against `test/requirements.txt`.

## Verification

The `functional` workflow on this PR runs the full browser e2e suite **without** the removed installs; a green run confirms no running test needed bokeh/plotly/opencv. (No repro demo applies — this is a CI/setup change.)

prs.title: ci: speed up functional tests + frontend profiling
prs.body:
Speeds up the two slowest frontend-related CI workflows.

## 1. `functional` workflow: ~10.5 min/leg → ~3.8 min slowest leg

Before, one leg ([run](https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/actions/runs/28389062296)): `install 302s` (a ~197s `pnpm build` run independently in **both** SSR legs + ~80s website-doc generation browser tests don't need) + `browser tests 207s` (only 4 workers on a 16-core runner) + `reload 98s` (run **redundantly in both legs** — reload never sets `GRADIO_SSR_MODE`).

- **Build the frontend once** in a shared `build` job; both SSR legs download `gradio/templates/**` as an artifact instead of each rebuilding it. The build needs only the checked-out repo + node (no Python).
- **Skip website-doc generation** in the test legs via a new `skip_docs_gen` input on the shared `install-all-deps` action (default `"false"`, so the 6 other callers are unchanged) — install dropped from **302s → 48s**.
- **8 browser workers** (was 4) via a scoped `PW_BROWSER_WORKERS` env (default stays 4, so storybook/snapshot runs are unaffected).
- **Reload tests get their own leg** (`functional-reload`) instead of running after the browser suite in both SSR legs. Browser legs keep their exact check names (`functional-test-SSR=true/false`).

Result with all four changes active ([run](https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/actions/runs/28391599838), all ✅): `build 0.5m`, `SSR=true 3.8m`, `SSR=false 3.2m`, `reload 2.5m`.

> Note: `skip_docs_gen` is a new input on the `@main` `install-all-deps` action, so it only takes effect **after this PR merges** (the current `@main` action ignores the unknown input). Until then the test legs still run doc-gen (~80s) — the other three changes apply immediately.

## 2. `frontend-profiling` workflow: ~9.9 min → ~5.6 min, every run

The benchmark built the frontend twice (~4 min each, [run](https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/actions/runs/28391006327)): once for the latest **release tag** ("base") and once for the PR — the benchmarks themselves take ~25s total.

- **Install the base from the published PyPI wheel** instead of checking out the tag and rebuilding it. The release wheel already ships the built frontend, so the base side drops the ~4min `pnpm build` entirely — on every run, no cache. The job stays on the PR checkout (benchmark spec + demo are the PR's for both runs); the demo is launched as `python <runner>.py` (runner/demo dir on `sys.path`, not cwd), so `import gradio` resolves to the installed package — the wheel for base, the editable build for PR. Base and PR use separate venvs so the editable install can't shadow the base wheel.

Result ([run](https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/actions/runs/28397018596), ✅): base side ~40s (wheel install + deps + benchmark, no build); the remaining 235s is the PR build (the artifact being measured). `base benchmark` and `compare` both pass, confirming the wheel base produces a valid measurement.

data flow before building. Comment inline on the doc.

### What it proposes

A way for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, …) to get a human back in the loop:

```bash
gradio --wait-for-result app.py
```

1. Agent writes a quick Gradio app that shows examples (with normal flagging).
2. The command launches it and **blocks**.
3. Human flags examples, clicks **"Finish & send results"** (or closes the tab).
4. Flagged rows come back to the agent as JSON on stdout.

No code change to the app is required — the flag is sugar over a `GRADIO_WAIT_FOR_RESULT`
env var, which is sugar over a `launch(wait_for_result=True)` kwarg (mirrors the existing
`GRADIO_MCP_SERVER` pattern).

### Reuses existing primitives

- **Flagging** (`gradio/flagging.py`) as the "mark examples to send back" mechanism — add an in-memory sink.
- **`unload`/heartbeat** (`routes.py:1234`) as the tab-close fallback.
- **`block_thread()`** (`blocks.py:3361`) for the blocking-until-finish wait.

The new piece is a "block until the human is done, then return the collected data" path,
plus a floating "Finish" button rendered as app chrome.

### Open questions in the doc

1. Return channel: stdout sentinels vs. `--result-file`.
2. Scope of "the data" for non-flagging apps (proposed: flagging-only for v1).
3. Finish button: overlay chrome vs. requiring a `gr.Button` (proposed: overlay).
4. Naming bikeshed.

See **`rfcs/wait-for-result.md`** for the full plan, architecture diagram, file-by-file
breakdown, and suggested build order.

prs.title: Fix embedded apps growing infinitely tall on Spaces
prs.body:
We've had many reports of embedded Gradio apps growing **infinitely tall** on HF Spaces, including these two:
- **#12089** — a component height set with `vh`/`%` units grows without bound (regressed between v5.34 and v5.49).
- **#12992** — `fill_height` apps grow without bound when launched with `footer_links=[]` (since 6.9.0).

## Root cause and fix

When embedded on Spaces, the app reports its own height via `parentIFrame.size()` from a `ResizeObserver` on the root container (`js/core/src/Blocks.svelte`). Content sized in `vh`/`%`, or stretched by `fill_height`, grows to fill whatever height the iframe is given — so its measured bottom just **tracks the viewport**. The unconditional `+ 32` padding then makes every report larger than the last, so each report grows the iframe → grows the content → triggers another report: an unbounded feedback loop. The closing `ResizeObserver` was added in #11919 (v5.49); `fill_height` being restored in #12956 (6.9.0) supplied a second elastic-content trigger; and `footer_links=[]` removed the footer slack that had been masking it.

> For `fill_height` (#12992) the divergence is **start-height dependent**: at a small iframe height the content doesn't fully fill, leaving a stabilizing gap, so it only runs away once the iframe is tall enough to be fully filled — which is exactly the case on a real Space, and why it doesn't reproduce when you run the app directly.

**1. `handle_resize` (`js/core/src/Blocks.svelte`)** now:
1. **skips growth when content merely fills the viewport** (no genuine overflow),
2. **ignores sub-pixel echoes** from our own resize, and
3. trips a **circuit breaker** after several consecutive grows (a self-induced loop), so the reported height stays bounded.

## Verification

This Space demonstrates the issue: https://huggingface.co/spaces/abidlabs/embed-height-bug-12089
Same Space but with this wheel no longer has the issue: https://huggingface.co/spaces/abidlabs/embed-height-bug-12089-fixed

Closes #12089
Closes #12992

prs.title: Add `allowed_origins` to restrict CORS access
prs.body:
## Description

Gradio's built-in `CustomCORSMiddleware` only ever enforced a **localhost CSRF guard**. On any non-localhost host (a deployed app, a LAN host, an `hf.space`) it reflected *whatever* `Origin` the request sent back into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` — and there was **no supported way to restrict which origins may make cross-origin requests** (#10276). Adding your own `CORSMiddleware` after `mount_gradio_app` doesn't help, because Gradio's middleware still writes the reflected header. `mount_gradio_app` also never forwarded `strict_cors` at all.

## Change

Add an `allowed_origins: list[str] | None = None` parameter to:
- `Blocks.launch()`
- `gradio.mount_gradio_app()` (which now also forwards `strict_cors`)
- `App.create_app()` → `CustomCORSMiddleware`

When set, only those exact origins are reflected in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, regardless of the server host. When unset (default), behavior is unchanged (localhost CSRF protection + origin reflection).

```python
demo.launch(allowed_origins=["https://example.com"])
```

## Verification

New test `test_allowed_origins_cors_restrictions` + existing CORS tests pass. Manual curl against a non-localhost `Host`:

| request | before | after (`allowed_origins=["https://example.com"]`) |
|---|---|---|
| `Origin: https://evil.com` | `ACAO: https://evil.com` (reflected) | no `ACAO` header (blocked) |
| `Origin: https://example.com` | reflected | `ACAO: https://example.com` |

Scoped to #10276. The related #5117 (CSP / `X-Frame-Options` to disable *framing*) is a distinct mechanism — its frontend "respect CSP" half is gated on Spaces emitting the header — and is left as a follow-up that can build on this.

Closes #10276

prs.title: Fix `this.app.$destroy is not a function` in the `<gradio-app>` web component
prs.body:
I've started workthough the issues related to embedding Gradio apps. This is a small bug fix: embedding a Gradio app with the `<gradio-app>` web component could throw:

```
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: this.app.$destroy is not a function
```

The custom element's `connectedCallback` (`js/spa/src/main.ts`) still called the **Svelte 4** `this.app.$destroy()` API. After the Svelte 5 migration the app is created with `mount(...)`, which returns an object with no `$destroy()` method — it must be torn down with `unmount()`. So whenever `connectedCallback` ran with `this.app` already set (the element was reconnected — moved in the DOM, or detached and re-attached), it threw and left the embed broken.

`attributeChangedCallback` already uses the correct Svelte 5 `unmount(this.app)`; this just makes `connectedCallback` consistent.

```diff
 			if (this.app) {
-				this.app.$destroy();
+				unmount(this.app);
 			}
```


I added an e2e regression test (`js/spa/test/web_component_embed.spec.ts` + `demo/web_component_embed`) that embeds the app via the web component, detaches/re-attaches it, and asserts no `$destroy` error and that the app re-renders. An e2e regression test might be a bit much for a small bug like this, but I'm planning on expanding this e2e test as I fix the other embedding-related issues.

Closes #12507

prs.title: Fix `select` event not firing on the `gr.Tabs` container
prs.body:
I noticed this bug when investigating #3793. Basically, that issue should have been closed since we should have supported Tabs + select, but this behavior wasn't working: The `select` event on a **`gr.Tabs` container** (`tabs.select(...)`) never fired when the user switched tabs

### Root cause

In the frontend event dispatcher (`js/core/src/Blocks.svelte`), a Tabs `select` event had its target id **overwritten** with the selected child tab's logical `id`:

```js
if (event === "select" && id in app_tree.initial_tabs) {
    id = (data as { id: number }).id;   // redirected away from the Tabs container
}
```

Two problems:

1. **`tabs.select(...)` never fired** — the dispatch was redirected off the Tabs container, so a listener on the container itself never matched its dependency.
2. **`TabItem.select(...)` was unreliable** — it used the tab's *user-facing* `id`. That only happens to equal the component id when no explicit id is set; with `gr.Tab("A", id="a")` the string `"a"` matched no component, so the per-tab `select` only worked for tabs without an explicit `id`.

### Fix

Dispatch the `select` event to **both**:
- the selected **TabItem**, keyed by `data.component_id` (which always identifies the component, regardless of an explicit string `id`), and
- the original **Tabs container** id,

so listeners on either fire correctly.

### Verification

```py
import gradio as gr

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    gr.Markdown("## Use the selected tab as an input")

    with gr.Tabs() as tabs:
        with gr.Tab("Celsius", id="celsius"):
            gr.Markdown("Temperatures are interpreted as °C.")
        with gr.Tab("Fahrenheit", id="fahrenheit"):
            gr.Markdown("Temperatures are interpreted as °F.")

    temp = gr.Number(label="Temperature", value=100)
    result = gr.Textbox(label="Converted to the other unit")

    def convert(temp, evt: gr.SelectData):
        if evt.value == "Celsius":
            return f"{temp}°C = {temp * 9 / 5 + 32:.1f}°F"
        return f"{temp}°F = {(temp - 32) * 5 / 9:.1f}°C"

    tabs.select(convert, inputs=temp, outputs=result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo.launch()
```

which lets use close: #3793


Added an e2e test (`js/spa/test/tabs.spec.ts`) covering the container-level `select` event, with a corresponding `outer_tabs.select(...)` in `demo/tabs`.

prs.title: Replace deprecated Starlette 422 status constant in queue validator error path
prs.body:
Starlette deprecated `HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` in favor of `HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT`, which surfaces a deprecation warning during normal Gradio import/use paths. This PR updates Gradio’s queue validator error mapping to the non-deprecated constant and adds targeted coverage for that path.

- **Queue validator error status mapping**
  - Updated `/queue/join` error mapping in `gradio/routes.py`:
    - `validator_error` now maps to `status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT` instead of the deprecated `status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY`.
  - Behavior remains `422`; only the deprecated symbol usage is removed.

- **Regression coverage for deprecation safety**
  - Added a focused test in `test/test_routes.py` to assert the validator-error branch:
    - returns HTTP `422`
    - does not emit `StarletteDeprecationWarning` for the old constant

```python
error_map = {
    "queue_full": status.HTTP_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
    "validator_error": status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
    "error": status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
    "success": status.HTTP_200_OK,
}
```

prs.title: Fix Column staying hidden after a multi-yield visibility update
prs.body:
## Description

A `gr.Column` that starts with `visible=False` could stay hidden even after an event handler updated it to `visible=True`, when the handler was a generator that yielded visibility updates more than once and another component's visibility changed in the same event.

Minimal reproduction (from #13494):

```python
import gradio as gr

def next_():
    yield gr.update(visible=False), gr.update(visible=False)
    yield gr.update(visible=False), gr.update(visible=True)

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    with gr.Column() as a:
        button = gr.Button("Next")
    with gr.Column(visible=False) as b:
        gr.Markdown("Doesn't appear")
    button.click(next_, outputs=[a, b])

demo.launch()
```

Clicking `Next` should reveal column `b`, but it stayed hidden.

Root cause: a column that starts hidden is not mounted (it is lazily loaded when it becomes visible). While it is unmounted, `update_state` stores its updates in a `pending` map. The first yield stores `pending = {visible: false}`. On the second yield, `load_components` mounts the column and `register_component` runs during the same `await tick()`, reading that now-stale `pending = {visible: false}` and scheduling it to be applied on the next microtask. `update_state` then applies the correct `visible: true` directly, but the deferred stale `visible: false` fires afterwards and overwrites it, so the column ends up hidden.

The fix: stop storing `visible` in the pending map at all (in `update_state`), the same way `loading_status` is already excluded. `visible` is the source of truth for whether a component mounts and is kept current in place on the node, and a mounted component syncs `visible` from the node props on mount, so it never needs to be replayed via a deferred `_set_data`. Storing it only allowed the stale earlier-yield value to overwrite the already-correct mounted state. This is the same class of stale-overwrite that `loading_status` is already protected from in this code path.

Closes: #13494

## AI Disclosure

- [x] I used AI to investigate the root cause and implement the fix.
- [ ] I did not use AI
## 🎯 PRs Should Target Issues

Before your create a PR, please check to see if there is [an existing issue](https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/issues) for this change. If not, please create an issue before you create this PR, unless the fix is very small. 

Not adhering to this guideline will result in the PR being closed. 

## Testing and Formatting Your Code

1. PRs will only be merged if tests pass on CI. We recommend at least running the backend tests locally, please set up [your Gradio environment locally](https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and run the backed tests: `bash scripts/run_backend_tests.sh`

2. Please run these bash scripts to automatically format your code: `bash scripts/format_backend.sh`, and (if you made any changes to non-Python files) `bash scripts/format_frontend.sh`

prs.title: Fix website-build: handle missing versioned templates for python-client and third-party-clients docs
prs.body:
Versioned docs pages like `/4.44.1/docs/python-client/introduction` were returning 500 errors during prerender because older S3 template archives don't include `python-client` or `third-party-clients` SVX templates, leaving `module` as `undefined` and crashing on `data.module.default`.

## Changes

- **`python-client/[doc]/+page.ts`** and **`third-party-clients/[doc]/+page.ts`**: Added two-stage fallback when loading templates:
  1. Try versioned template (e.g. `templates_4-44-1/`) — existing behavior
  2. Fall back to main unversioned templates (`templates/`, explicitly excluding `templates_*`) when no versioned match found
  3. Throw `404` if neither exists, rather than returning `undefined` and crashing in the component

This mirrors the pattern already in `gradio/[doc]/+page.ts`, which had proper undefined-module handling.

prs.title: Make dropdowns accessible to screen readers (combobox ARIA pattern)
prs.body:
## Description

Gradio dropdowns are currently unusable with screen readers such as NVDA and JAWS. The text `<input>` is given `role="listbox"`, which is the wrong ARIA role: a listbox is a container of options, not a text field. Screen readers receive contradictory signals (an element that announces as a list but behaves as an editable text field), so users cannot tell what the control is. On top of that, the input has no `aria-activedescendant`, so when the user arrows through the popup the screen reader only re-reads the input's current value and never announces the option names. The net effect is that blind users cannot select anything from any Gradio dropdown, which blocks a large number of Gradio apps.

This switches the dropdown to the standard WAI-ARIA combobox pattern:

- The input now uses `role="combobox"` instead of `role="listbox"`.
- `aria-activedescendant` points at the id of the currently highlighted option while the list is open, so the screen reader announces each option as the user navigates with the arrow keys (DOM focus stays in the input, as the pattern requires).
- `aria-autocomplete` is set (`list` when the dropdown is filterable, `none` otherwise) to describe the filtering behavior.

The popup itself was already correct (`<ul role="listbox">` with `<li role="option" aria-selected>`), so no markup changes were needed there. The existing `aria-controls` / `aria-expanded` wiring is kept.

The same fix is applied to the multiselect variant, which previously had no combobox semantics on its input at all (no role, no `aria-controls`/`aria-expanded`, no `aria-activedescendant`). It now also passes a `listbox_id` to the shared options list so the options have stable ids to reference.

This addresses two issues that describe the same underlying problem: #10532 (single-select `gr.Dropdown`) and #12855 (Gradio's listboxes/comboboxes not usable with a screen reader, which also covers the multiselect case noted by a maintainer there). Fixing both the single-select and multiselect inputs closes both.

Closes: #10532
Closes: #12855

## Testing

- The added unit tests in `js/dropdown/dropdown.test.ts` fail on the unpatched code and pass with the fix, so they pin the regression rather than just asserting the current state.
- Manually verified with VoiceOver on macOS (Safari): the dropdown is now announced as a combobox and each option is read out as you arrow through the list.

prs.title: Fix long unbroken text overflowing in the Markdown component
prs.body: ## Description Long unbreakable strings (a long URL, an underscore-joined token) did not wrap in markdown: they overflowed the container horizontally, and in list items the bullet/number marker was pushed onto its own line. This is the remaining part of #7844. - `js/markdown-code/MarkdownCode.svelte`: add `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to the markdown span so the text wraps. `anywhere` (not `break-word`) also lowers min-content width, so markdown wraps inside table cells and flex items rather than forcing them to overflow. Code blocks keep `word-wrap: normal` and still scroll. - `js/theme/src/typography.css`: switch `.prose` lists from `inside` to `outside` markers (with a padding gutter) so the marker stays beside the first line when a long item wraps. Both edits are on the shared markdown path, so the fix applies to the Markdown component, Chatbot messages, and Dataframe markdown cells. Note it changes list rendering everywhere `.prose` is used: markers now sit in a gutter with a standard hanging indent. Closes: #7844 ## Screenshots | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | App used for the screenshots: ```python import gradio as gr LONG = "long_text_" * 25 md = f"""# Heading: {LONG} - {LONG} - a normal short item A long URL: https://example.com/{"very_long_path/" * 15}end """ with gr.Blocks() as demo: with gr.Group(): gr.Markdown(md) gr.Chatbot(value=[{"role": "assistant", "content": md}], height=500) demo.launch() ``` ## Testing Verified in Storybook and by running Gradio apps: the Markdown component (lists, long URL), Chatbot messages, and Dataframe markdown cells, plus markdown in narrow and uneven `Column`s to check the min-content effect. In each case the text wraps within its container, list markers align with their text, nothing overflows horizontally, and no column collapsed. prs.title: Fix gr.Plot collapsing to zero height for autosize Plotly figures
prs.body:
## Description

A `gr.Plot` showing a Plotly figure with no explicit `layout.height` (i.e. relying on autosize) rendered at zero height in 6.18.0, leaving the plot area blank. A fixed `height` avoided it. This was a regression from #13510 ("Migrate Plot to Svelte 5").

The migration moved the draw logic in `js/plot/shared/plot_types/PlotlyPlot.svelte` from `afterUpdate` to a `$effect`. That effect calls `load_plotly_css()`, which both reads (`if (!loaded_plotly_css)`) and writes (`loaded_plotly_css = true`) the `$bindable` `loaded_plotly_css` state. Writing a tracked dependency from inside the effect re-invalidates it, so the effect runs twice. The first `Plotly.react` establishes the autosize default height (450px); the second re-applies the responsive layout and collapses the container back to zero height. Svelte 4's `afterUpdate` was never dependency-tracked, so it did not self-retrigger.

The fix wraps the one-time CSS load in `untrack(...)` so `loaded_plotly_css` is no longer a dependency of the effect. The effect then runs once per `plot`/`show_label` change, and the bindable write still propagates to the parent for cross-instance CSS deduplication. This is the same `untrack` idiom that `AltairPlot.svelte` already uses (around its `old_spec`/`spec_width` writes) and that was introduced in the same migration PR.

Closes: #13539

prs.title: Use OAuth fallback for workflow text generation
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes workflow text-generation calls so they only use browser-side streaming when the frontend has an HF token. If no frontend token is available, the workflow executor now falls back to the backend `call_model` path, where Gradio can inject the logged-in user's OAuth token and use their inference provider credits.

Also adds regression coverage that an empty manual token slot does not block OAuth or local write-token fallback on the backend.

Closes: #13536

prs.author: gradio-pr-bot

prs.title: Re-translate i18n choices display names when the language is switched at runtime
prs.body:
## Description

Since #13516, `gr.I18n` markers in the `choices` of choice-based components (Radio, CheckboxGroup, Dropdown, SimpleDropdown) are translated on initial load. However, switching the language at runtime (Settings -> Language) only updated scalar props such as `label` and `info`, leaving the choice display names in the previous locale.

This PR makes choice display names follow runtime language switches:

- Adds `Gradio.live_i18n()` in `@gradio/utils`. It wraps the injected `i18n_store` with Svelte's `fromStore()`, so reading it inside a derived or a template subscribes that caller to locale changes. When no store is injected (for example the unit test render helper), it falls back to the construction-time `gradio.i18n`.
- Switches the choice render sites in CheckboxGroup, Radio, Dropdown (single and multiselect) and SimpleDropdown from `gradio.i18n(...)` to `gradio.live_i18n(...)`. Other inline `gradio.i18n(...)` call sites (fallback labels, tooltips) are intentionally left as is to keep the diff scoped to choices; they can be migrated in a follow-up if useful.
- Fixes SimpleDropdown clearing its value when the display strings change underneath it (which is exactly what happens on a locale switch): the display-to-value reverse lookup now re-derives the displayed string from the still-valid internal value before falling back to clearing the selection.

Design note: a shared `$state` counter bumped from the `i18n_store` subscription in the `Gradio` class was tried first and caused an infinite reactive loop in the real app. The `fromStore()` approach keeps the subscription local to each caller, with no shared mutable state. It also deliberately avoids funneling the store value through an intermediate `$derived`: deriveds short-circuit on reference equality and the emitted formatter reference never changes, so propagation would stop there.

Tests:

- Runtime-switch unit tests in all four component suites. prs.title: Fix fullscreen button not working in ImageSlider, interactive Image, native plots, and AnnotatedImage
prs.body:
## Description

The fullscreen button does nothing when clicked in four components: `gr.ImageSlider`, interactive `gr.Image`, native plots (`gr.LinePlot`, `gr.ScatterPlot`, `gr.BarPlot`), and `gr.AnnotatedImage`. The browser console shows `Uncaught TypeError: e.onclick is not a function`.

The shared `FullscreenButton` atom changed its API in the Svelte 5 migration (#12779): it used to dispatch a `fullscreen` event, and now requires an `onclick: (fullscreen: boolean) => void` prop. Four call sites were never updated and still used the old `on:fullscreen` wiring, so `onclick` was undefined and clicking threw. The static `gr.Image` and Gallery instances of this bug were fixed earlier in #13004 and #12865; this PR updates the remaining call sites the same way:

- `js/imageslider/shared/SliderPreview.svelte` and `js/image/shared/ImageUploader.svelte`: wire `onclick` to update the local `fullscreen` state and dispatch a component-level `fullscreen` event, which their parent `Index.svelte` files already listen for (same pattern as the ImagePreview fix in #13004).
- `js/nativeplot/Index.svelte` and `js/annotatedimage/Index.svelte`: replace the inline `on:fullscreen` handler with an `onclick` handler (same pattern as `js/plot/Index.svelte`).

In nativeplot, the now-working fullscreen toggle re-renders the chart and exposed a small race in `load_chart`: the function can resume from `await import("vega-embed")` after the component has unmounted, calling `vegaEmbed` with a null element and producing an unhandled promise rejection. Added a null check after the await.

Each component gets a unit test that clicks the fullscreen button and asserts the mode toggles on and off. All four tests fail on `main` with the `onclick is not a function` error and pass with this fix.

Note: the 2026 comments on #10268 reporting that the fullscreen button "does nothing" on `gr.Image` are the interactive-Image instance of this bug and are fixed here as well (the coordinate issue that #10268 is actually about is being addressed separately).

prs.title: Fix `gr.SelectData` coordinates when the image in `gr.Image` does not fill its container
prs.body:
## Description

When the image shown in `gr.Image` is smaller than its display box, the x/y coordinates reported through `gr.SelectData` are wrong. This is most visible in fullscreen mode: the display box grows to the viewport size while the image stays at its natural size (it is intentionally not upscaled to avoid blurriness), and clicks are reported as if the image had been stretched to fill the screen.

The root cause is a mismatch between the CSS and the coordinate math. The image is rendered with `object-fit: scale-down`, which never enlarges the image beyond its natural size, so a small image is centered with empty space on both axes. But `get_coordinates_of_clicked_image()` assumed `object-fit: contain` behavior, where the image always fills the box along at least one axis and empty space can only appear along one axis. Whenever the box is larger than the image in both dimensions, that assumption breaks and the computed coordinates are scaled and offset incorrectly.

This was previously fixed in #10901 by changing the CSS so the container hugged the image, but that broke scaling when `height=` is set (#10991) and was reverted in #11091. This PR instead leaves the CSS untouched and fixes the math: the displayed image rect is computed with scale-down semantics (`scale = min(box_w / natural_w, box_h / natural_h, 1)`, centered on both axes) and the click position is inverted from that. The two existing code branches (landscape/portrait letterboxing) are special cases of this formula, so behavior is unchanged in the cases that already worked, which the existing unit tests confirm. Clicks landing in the empty space around the image now return no coordinates (no `select` event), matching the existing behavior for clicks outside the image bounds.

Added unit tests for the natural-size-centered case (including a fullscreen-sized box) and for clicks in the surrounding empty space, which fail on `main`.

Closes: #10268

prs.title: Wait for in-flight head scripts before running js_on_load in gr.HTML
prs.body:
## Description

When two gr.HTML components on the same page declare the same external script in `head`, only the first one works on initial page load. The first instance appends the `<script>` tag and awaits its `onload` before running `js_on_load`. The second instance's dedupe check in `loadHead()` finds the tag already in `document.scripts` and skips it, but it has no way to wait for that in-flight load, so its `js_on_load` runs immediately and fails with errors like `ReferenceError: $3Dmol is not defined`. After a hot-reload re-render the script is already loaded, which is why the bug seemed to disappear until the next browser refresh.

This PR adds a module-level map from script `src` to its load promise. When an instance appends a head script it registers the promise, and any later instance that dedupes the same `src` awaits that promise before running `js_on_load`. Scripts that are already in the document but were not added through `loadHead()` (for example, scripts in the served page itself) keep the current skip behavior.

Also declares the missing `head` prop in the component's props type annotation, which fixes a pre-existing svelte-check error in this file.

Added a Playwright test (`html_head_script_shared.spec.ts` with the `html_head_script_shared` demo fixture) that renders two gr.HTML components sharing one delayed head script and asserts both `js_on_load` callbacks see the library. The test fails without the fix (the second component runs too early) and passes with it. The existing `html_head_script_order` and `html_head_script_async` tests still pass, so the document-order and explicit-async behavior from #13450 is preserved.

Closes: #13528

prs.title: Close matplotlib figures after rendering them in `gr.Plot`
prs.body:
## Description

Matplotlib figures returned to `gr.Plot` were never closed after being encoded, so every event that updated a plot left another open figure in pyplot's global registry. Long-running apps accumulated figures, leaked memory, and eventually triggered matplotlib's "More than 20 figures have been opened" warning.

`Plot.postprocess` now calls `plt.close(value)` once the figure has been encoded to base64. Only `Figure` instances are closed. The legacy path where a handler returns the `pyplot` module itself is left untouched, since closing the current figure there could break apps that keep drawing on it across calls.

Closing a figure does not prevent it from being rendered again: `savefig` still works on a closed figure, so apps that hold on to a figure (for example in `gr.State`) and return it to `gr.Plot` repeatedly keep working. A test covers this, along with a regression test that the figure registry stays empty after `postprocess`. Figures created directly via `matplotlib.figure.Figure` (not through pyplot) are not in the registry, and closing them is a no-op.

Closes: #11701

prs.title: Fix UI freeze when one event makes multiple components of the same type visible
prs.body:
## Description

When a single event listener flipped two or more components of the same type from `visible=False` to `visible=True` (e.g. two sliders, two textboxes, two images), the page froze: the main thread locked up, the UI never updated, and the tab eventually crashed out of memory. No error appeared on the backend or in the browser console.

```python
import gradio as gr

def show():
    return gr.update(visible=True), gr.update(visible=True)

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    btn = gr.Button("Show")
    s1 = gr.Slider(0, 1, value=0, visible=False)
    s2 = gr.Slider(0, 1, value=0, visible=False)
    btn.click(show, None, [s1, s2])

demo.launch()
```

### Root cause

For a visibility update on a not-yet-loaded component, `AppTree.update_state()` rebuilt the entire component tree with `traverse()` and reassigned `this.root`. The rebuild gives every node in the tree a new `children` array. `DependencyManager.handle_data()` applies outputs in parallel (`Promise.all`), so one event with two visibility outputs runs two of these whole-tree rebuilds concurrently, interleaved around `await tick()`. Components of the same type also share one cached loading promise (`load_component`'s `request_map`), which `MountComponents.svelte` consumes via `$derived(await node.component)`. The combination (two racing whole-tree rebuilds under an already-mounted parent, plus two async deriveds awaiting the same promise) traps Svelte's async reactivity in a non-terminating update cycle. A CPU profile of the frozen page shows the main thread spinning inside Svelte's batch machinery (`Batch.apply`/`process`/`revive`).

I bisected the slider report to #12839 ("Hide forms with no elements", first released in 6.6.0). That PR did not introduce the cycle itself; by keeping forms mounted (hidden via CSS) instead of marking them invisible, it made the racing rebuilds happen under a mounted parent for form components, which is the common case from the issue (sliders, textboxes, numbers). The same freeze already existed before #12839 for components that are not wrapped in a form: making two `gr.Image` components visible in one event freezes 6.5.x as well. This fix addresses the shared root cause, so both cases are covered.

### Fix

Stop rebuilding the tree for visibility updates. `update_state()` now sets the target node's `visible` prop in place and loads any missing components in place via `load_components()`, the same pattern `render_previously_invisible_children()` already uses for programmatic accordion/tab expansion. Since nothing reassigns `this.root` or replaces `children` arrays anymore, concurrent visibility updates no longer interfere with each other.

Also fixed `load_components()` to store `get_component(...).component` (the loading promise) instead of the whole `{name, component, runtime}` return value, so `await node.component` in `MountComponents.svelte` resolves to the component module. The previous shape would render nothing if that branch were hit.

### Testing

- New Playwright test (`case two_sliders` in `js/spa/test/invisible_textbox.spec.ts` with `demo/invisible_textbox/two_sliders_testcase.py`): two same-type sliders made visible by one click. It times out on `main` (frozen page) and passes with this fix.
- Headless freeze probes (click "Show", then poll `page.evaluate`) against the fixed build: Slider x2, Textbox x3, Image x2, mixed Image+Textbox, and value-only updates are all responsive.
- Existing related suites pass: `invisible_textbox.spec.ts` (visibility toggling, forms, accordions from #12839/#12846), `visibility_test.spec.ts`, `tabs.spec.ts` (incl. lazy subtab/accordion loading from #12906), `accordion_tab_switch.spec.ts`, `tab_render_children.spec.ts`, and the `gr.render` suites (`render_merge`, `sub_block_render`, `render_queue_false`, `render_heavy_concurrently`).

Closes: #12995

prs.title: Use local HF token in Workflow, gated behind a write-token auth model
prs.body: ### Important changes (I wrote this): This PR: * Uses a user's logged-in HF token *when running Workflows locally* (not on Spaces since we probably don't want to expose the token in case it's saved as an env variable) * When run locally, there's a write-token that is generated. Only users with this write token will be able to change the workflow This prevents users who might access your app (e.g. via a share link) from editing the workflow.json file. * For users who don't have this write-token, they see a "read only" view instead, where they can only run the workflow, not edit it: * On Spaces, something similar happens. Take a Space like this: https://huggingface.co/spaces/abidlabs/wftest2. If you are not the owner of the Space (or don't have write permissions if the Space is owned by an org), then you get the read-only view (to prevent the issue that @AK391 experienced): * In order to edit the workflow, you just need to duplicate the Space under your own namespace or an org that you have access to. Open to feedback on this flow as well as the UI! --------- ### How it works (AI-generated) **Locally** (Jupyter/trackio-style): - A per-process `WRITE_TOKEN` (`secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, regenerated each process like a Jupyter notebook token) is generated, and `launch()` prints a private edit link: `http://127.0.0.1:7860/?write_token=…` (also used for `inbrowser=True`). - On page load the frontend moves the query param into a port-suffixed cookie and strips it from the URL; the server validates header → cookie → query param with `secrets.compare_digest`. **On Spaces:** write access requires OAuth as the Space owner, or an admin/write member of the owning org (whoami-based, cached via `huggingface_hub`). The write token is ignored on Spaces. **What write access gates (server-side):** - `get_token` only reveals the host's local HF token to write-access sessions; everyone else gets the logged-out experience and can paste their own PAT to run under their account. - The local-token fallback in `call_space` / `call_model` / `fetch_dataset` / search functions — guests can't consume the owner's quota or act under their identity. - `save_workflow` — rejected with an auth error otherwise. **Read-only UI:** a new `get_write_access` server function drives a view-only canvas for non-owners — a "View only" badge, with node/edge editing, renaming, clearing, auto-layout, and autosave disabled — while running the workflow and filling in input values remain fully functional. Token precedence is unchanged: manual token → OAuth → (write-access only) local token. Known limitation: notebook inline embeds (Jupyter/Colab iframes) load the plain local URL, so the embedded canvas is read-only; the printed edit link works in a browser tab. prs.title: Translate i18n `choices` display names in choice-based components
prs.body:
## Description

`gr.I18n` markers work for the `label` and `info` of choice-based components, but the `choices` display names were never translated. When a choice was supplied as `(i18n("bold"), "bold")`, the option rendered as the raw marker string (`__i18n__{"__type__":"translation_metadata","key":"bold"}`) instead of the translated text.

The i18n machinery only auto-translates a fixed allow-list of scalar props (`label`, `info`, etc.). `choices` is an array of `[display, value]` tuples, so it fell outside that path, and each component rendered the choice display value directly without passing it through the i18n formatter.

This PR routes the display side of each choice through the existing i18n formatter (`gradio.i18n`) at the point each component consumes its choices. Only the display name is translated; the internal value is left untouched, so event payloads and `value` handling are unchanged. Plain string choices are unaffected.

Covers all four choice-based components reported and adjacent:
- `CheckboxGroup`
- `Radio`
- `Dropdown` (single-select and multiselect)
- `SimpleDropdown`

For `Dropdown` and `SimpleDropdown`, the choices are translated once at the top of the data flow so that filtering, the selected-input text, the token labels, and the option list all stay consistent with the translated display names.

Closes: #11611

### Known limitation

This translates choices on initial load, which is what the issue reports. Re-translating choices on a runtime language switch (Settings → Language) is out of scope: `gradio.i18n` is set once per component and is not reactive to locale changes. The existing runtime-switch mechanism only covers scalar `translatable_props`.

The example tables rendered by `gr.Dataset` / `gr.Examples` (the per-component `Example.svelte` files) also display choice names raw, but those components are mounted without an i18n formatter, so translating them would require threading a formatter through the Dataset/Examples chain. That is left as a separate change.

prs.title: Fix state handling for simple call API
prs.body:
Fixes `/call/{api_name}` state handling for queued simple API calls by routing SSE reads through the original `session_hash` and padding omitted `State` inputs before queueing. This lets curl/bash-style requests keep server-side state across calls without clients needing to send state values.

Closes: #8452

Root cause: `/call/{api_name}/{event_id}` read queue messages using the event id as if it were the session hash, and the simple call body was passed to processing without placeholders for stateful inputs.

Here's what I did to confirm the fix. First, run this demo on, say, port 7864:

```python
import gradio as gr

def respond(message, history):
    history = history or []
    turn = len(history) // 2 + 1
    history = [*history, {"role": "user", "content": message}]
    history = [*history, {"role": "assistant", "content": f"Echo {turn}: {message}"}]
    return history, history

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    chatbot = gr.Chatbot()
    textbox = gr.Textbox()
    state = gr.State([])
    textbox.submit(respond, [textbox, state], [chatbot, state], api_name="chat")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo.queue().launch(server_port=7864, _frontend=False)
```

Then, make the following curl requests:

```bash
# First request
EVENT_ID=$(curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7864/gradio_api/call/chat \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data": ["Really?"], "session_hash": "randomsequence1234"}' \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["event_id"])')

curl -N http://127.0.0.1:7864/gradio_api/call/chat/$EVENT_ID

# Second request with the same session_hash
EVENT_ID=$(curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7864/gradio_api/call/chat \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data": ["Again?"], "session_hash": "randomsequence1234"}' \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["event_id"])')

curl -N http://127.0.0.1:7864/gradio_api/call/chat/$EVENT_ID
```

On this branch, the second response includes the first turn plus `Echo 2: Again?`, showing state persisted for `randomsequence1234`.

For comparison, I ran the exact same demo from current `origin/main` (`df590646a`) on port 7865 and made the same requests against `http://127.0.0.1:7865/gradio_api`:

```bash
# First request against main
EVENT_ID=$(curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7865/gradio_api/call/chat \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data": ["Really?"], "session_hash": "randomsequence1234"}' \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["event_id"])')

curl --max-time 5 -N http://127.0.0.1:7865/gradio_api/call/chat/$EVENT_ID

# Second request against main with the same session_hash
```

prs.title: Accept permanent redirects (301, 308) in `networking.url_ok`
prs.body:
## Description

`test/test_networking.py::TestURLs::test_url_ok` started failing because `https://www.gradio.app` now serves a **301** permanent redirect to `https://gradio.app/` (after the recent domain registrar migration). `url_ok` doesn't follow redirects and only accepted `200, 401, 302, 303, 307`, so the 301 was treated as a failure.

prs.title: Treat expired OAuth sessions as logged out users
prs.body:
#### Description

Expired OAuth session data was only cleared by `gr.LoginButton` when the page load check ran. Backend event handling still read the same expired `oauth_info` from the session and injected it into app functions as `gr.OAuthProfile` / `gr.OAuthToken`.

This adds a shared OAuth session helper used by both `LoginButton` and `helpers.special_args`: expired sessions are treated as logged out everywhere (no profile/token injection), and the stale `oauth_info` entry is removed from the session on the `LoginButton` page-load check (in the event path, `gr.Request` hands handlers a copy of the session, so removal there would not persist). Also stamps a fresh `expires_at` on each mocked local-dev login, since the previously startup-computed value made logins permanently expired after 8 hours of server uptime.

Closes: #6768

prs.title: Run `js` functions in event listeners even when `fn` is not explicitly set to `None`
prs.body:
Fixes #6729

#### Root cause

Event listeners (and `gr.on`) default `fn` to the `"decorator"` sentinel so they can be used as decorators. When `fn` was left unset, the call took the decorator branch and returned a no-op `Dependency` — so `btn.click(js=js)` silently registered no event at all, and the JS only ran if the user explicitly passed `fn=None`.

#### Fix

In the `"decorator"` branch of `EventListener._setup` and `gr.on`: if `js` is a string (a JS function can run entirely in the frontend without a backend `fn`), the event is registered immediately with `fn=None`. The returned `Dependency` still supports decorator usage — if it is applied to a function, the wrapper removes the eagerly-registered js-only event (restoring the fn id counter) and registers the decorated function instead, so `@btn.click(js=js)` continues to produce exactly one event with both the backend fn and the js. `js=True` (transpiled fn) is unaffected since it requires a real fn.

As a bonus, `btn.click(js=js)` now returns a real `Dependency`, so `.then()`/`.success()`/`.failure()` chaining works on js-only events.

Minimal repro demo:

```python
import gradio as gr

js = """
() => {
alert("js executed");
}
"""

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    with gr.Column():
        b1 = gr.Button("click me (js=js, fn=None)")
        b2 = gr.Button("click me (js=js only)")
        b3 = gr.Button("click me (gr.on, js=js only)")

    b1.click(js=js, fn=None)  # always worked
    b2.click(js=js)  # broken before fix
    gr.on(triggers=[b3.click], js=js)  # broken before fix without fn=None

demo.launch()
```

prs.title: Require brotli>=1.2.1 and refuse Brotli-encoded responses from user-supplied URLs
prs.body:
## Description

[CVE-2026-111497](https://www.aikido.dev/blog/python-packages-vulnerable-node2shell-brotli-cve-2026-111497) is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli **decoder**. It affects Brotli 1.0.3–1.2.0 (fixed in 1.2.1) and Node.js before 22.23.4 / 24.22.1 / 26.12.1. Decoding a crafted Brotli stream can crash the process or corrupt memory.

Gradio only uses brotli's `Compressor` (in `BrotliMiddleware`), so our own use of it isn't affected. But because Gradio depends on `brotli`, httpx in the same environment automatically decodes `Content-Encoding: br` responses. That includes the responses Gradio fetches from user-supplied URLs.

This PR:

- **Raises the floor to `brotli>=1.2.1`.** Our current `>=1.1.0` allows vulnerable releases.
- **Never Brotli-decodes responses from user-supplied URLs.** `async_ssrf_protected_get` (used for URL inputs, `gr.Audio` streaming, run history, and workflow providers) now does a streamed GET that:
  - keeps the same safehttpx IP validation and allow-list behavior;
  - sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate`;
  - refuses any response whose `Content-Encoding` includes `br` *before* httpx decodes the body.

  This is defense in depth, so the path stays closed even in environments with an older brotli or a future decoder bug.
- **Raises the Node `engines` floor to `>=24.22.1`.** Gradio's own Node code doesn't decode untrusted Brotli: the front proxy passes bytes through, and SSR `fetch()` only talks to the local Python backend. This floor is a precaution.

`/proxy=` and `/file=<url>` already stream with `aiter_raw()`, so they never decoded on the server and are unchanged.

No linked issue: this is a dependency/security fix for a public CVE.

## AI Disclosure

prs.title: Process executor: serve the app's config and an event table from the gateway
prs.body:
## Description

An alternative design for the process executor of #14003, for comparison. As there, `launch(executor="process")` (the default here) runs Gradio's server in a gateway process. The process that built the app runs every event, so models, globals and closures behave as they do with threads.

The difference is what the gateway knows about the app.

### How this differs from #14003

**In #14003, the gateway rebuilds the app.** It calls `Blocks.from_config` on the app's config, which creates every component, layout and event again as live Python objects. Gradio's routes and queue then run unchanged against that copy, and each event is forwarded to the app's process. This is why Gradio's core needed few changes. It is also where most of #14003's bugs came from:
- the config sent to browsers is regenerated from the copy;
- the copy runs component code (constructors, file caching, API info);
- whatever `from_config` doesn't carry over is lost.

Examples are Chatbot listener flags, `gr.HTML` props and events, subclasses defined in the app's script, `LoginButton`/OAuth and Dataset samples. Each needed its own fix, and custom components and `i18n` were still open (#14006).

**Here, the gateway never builds the app.** The app's process sends what the gateway serves, as data:
- **its config**, which the gateway serves to browsers as is;
- **its API info and theme CSS**;
- **an event table**: one `BlockFunction` per dependency in the config, plus the settings the config doesn't carry (concurrency, progress, validators). Its inputs and outputs are `AppBlock`s, which hold only an id and a type.

The gateway's queue schedules those events, and the gateway forwards "run event N" with the raw payload. The app's process preprocesses it, runs the function and postprocesses the result, so every component's logic stays there.

So the boundary is a small, fixed contract rather than a copy of the app that has to stay faithful:

| | #14003 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| The gateway's model of the app | A `Blocks` rebuilt with `from_config` | The app's config, API info and an event table |
| Config sent to browsers | Regenerated from the rebuilt components | The app's own, unchanged |
| Component code in the gateway | Constructors, `get_config`, file caching, API info | None |
| Subclasses, `gr.HTML`, themes from the app's script, `i18n` | Each needs a fix, or is refused | Nothing to do: they're in the config |
| MCP | The gateway's server, over the rebuilt app | The app's own server; the gateway forwards its routes |
| Changes to `from_config` | Many | None |

### What else is here
- **Replicas.** `GRADIO_PROCESS_REPLICAS=N` runs the app's script again N−1 times, which is how #13998 gets multi-core throughput.
  - A session stays on the process that first served it, since its state and generators live there; new sessions go to the least busy one.
  - `concurrency_limit` applies per process.
  - `GET /gradio_api/processes` lists the processes.
  - There's no autoscaler; that's #13998's policy and could sit on top of this.
- **From #14003:** the request plumbing and lifecycle handling come over as they are. That covers auth, OAuth sessions, FastAPI dependencies, `auth_dependency` request state, lifespans, a Server's own routes and websockets, run history, `delete_cache`, startup events and the gateway's shutdown.
- **Defaults:** `executor="process"` is the default, so the whole test suite and the e2e tests run against it. Reload mode still falls back to threads.

### Not done yet
- `gr.render` is refused. With this design, the gateway would add the events of a re-render to the session's event table from the app's config updates, without building anything. The e2e specs that use it run with threads.
- A Server's middleware is refused, as in #14003.
- Routes forwarded to the app (component server functions, deep links, media streams) go to the first process, not to the session's replica.
- The messages between the processes are still pickled Python objects, as in #14003. A network-safe format (JSON plus files by value) is the step that would let the app's process run on another machine.

Benchmarks against thread mode, #14003 and #13998 are in a comment below.

Closes: #14013

## AI Disclosure

- [x] I used AI to... design and write this PR with Claude Code: the code, the tests, the benchmarks and this description. I reviewed it and directed the design.
- [ ] I did not use AI

## Testing and Formatting Your Code

- `test/test_process_executor.py`: 26 tests, including OAuth, Server routes and dependencies, validators, `auth_dependency` state, lifespans, and classes and themes defined in the app's script.
- The rest of the backend suite passes in process mode (the new default), apart from the Docker reverse-proxy tests, which need Docker.
- The Playwright suite passes locally with the new default: 221 passed and 2 flaky, the reload specs included. The `gr.render` demos run with threads.
- Formatted with `scripts/format_backend.sh` and `scripts/format_frontend.sh`.

## Deploying the ML side separately

This design is a better base for running the app's functions on another machine (say, a GPU job) than the UI, though it doesn't do that yet. The gateway never imports the app or its components: it needs only Gradio and the data the app's process sends. So the boundary is a small contract ("run event N with this payload") rather than a copy of the app, which a UI host would otherwise need the app's code and component classes to rebuild, as in #14003.

What still ties both sides to one machine:
1. **Transport:** a plaintext loopback socket protected by a token. It would need TLS, and probably the worker dialing out to the gateway.
2. **Serialization:** pickled Python objects instead of a JSON or msgpack schema.
3. **Files:** passed as paths on a shared disk, not sent by value.
4. **Lifecycle:** the app's process spawns the gateway and the gateway follows its pid, instead of each side starting and reconnecting on its own.
5. **Forwarded routes:** component server functions, deep links, media streams, MCP and a Server's own routes go to a loopback port.

prs.title: Remove `gr.Column` and `gr.Row` variants
prs.body:
## Description

Removes the `variant` parameter from `gr.Column` and `gr.Row` in Gradio 7, as suggested in the issue thread. This is a breaking change: passing `variant` (any value, including `"default"`) now raises `TypeError: Column.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'variant'`.

Before this PR, both layouts had three variants:
- `"default"`: no styling. This was the default.
- `"panel"`: rounded corners, a background and padding. Column's panel also had a border and used `--panel-background-fill`. Row's panel had no border and used `--background-fill-secondary`, so the two didn't match.
- `"compact"`: the same look as `panel`, but it also set children's border radii to 0 and turned off the automatic `Form` grouping of adjacent form components. That second effect changed layout behavior from a styling option, and it was hard to discover.

Both non-default variants only changed how the layout looked, and `elem_classes` with custom CSS covers that.

### Migration

Remove `variant=...`. To get the panel look back, add a class and style it with the theme's panel variables, so it still follows the theme and dark mode:

```python
css = """
.my-panel {
    border: solid var(--panel-border-width) var(--panel-border-color);
    border-radius: var(--container-radius);
    background: var(--panel-background-fill);
    padding: var(--spacing-lg);
}
"""
with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    with gr.Column(elem_classes="my-panel"):
        ...
demo.launch(css=css)
```

### Changes

Backend:
- Removed `variant` from `gr.Column` and `gr.Row`, including the `compact` logic that turned off `Form` grouping. Since nothing else set `allow_expected_parents`, that check is removed from `BlockContext.__exit__`.

Frontend:
- Removed the `variant` prop and `.panel` / `.compact` styles from `@gradio/column` and `@gradio/row`. Also removed `@gradio/column`'s unused `Index.svelte` style block.
- The login page (`@gradio/core`) used `<BaseColumn variant="panel">`. It now uses an `elem_classes` class with the same styles.

Internal usages:
- The theme preview apps (`gradio/themes/app.py`, `gradio/themes/builder_app.py` and `gr.themes.builder()`) use `elem_classes="panel"` plus a `.panel` CSS rule, so theme authors still see the `panel_*` theme variables, which are unchanged.
- Removed `variant` from the `audio_mixer` and `shared_props` demos, and the matching assertions from `shared_props.spec.ts`.

Tests:
- Passing `variant` to Column or Row raises `TypeError`.
- Column and Row don't send `variant` in their config and still group adjacent Textboxes into a `Form`.

## Before / after

Each Space shows `gr.Column()` / `gr.Row()` plus every `variant` value around two Textboxes, a Slider and a Button.

- **Before** (gradio 6.30.0 from PyPI): https://huggingface.co/spaces/dawood/layout-variants-before. `panel` and `compact` are styled.
- **After** (this PR's `7.0.0.dev0` preview wheel, run as a Docker Space): https://huggingface.co/spaces/dawood/layout-variants-after. The plain layouts render, and every `variant=` call shows the `TypeError` it raises.

Closes: #13651

prs.title: Add a process executor that runs the server in a separate gateway process
prs.body:
This big, beautiful PR changes how Gradio runs: now when you launch a Gradio app, the Gradio web server **runs in a separate "gateway" process**. The main process continues to run the model, every function that the user defined, etc. 

The downsides are: (1) slightly more memory usage because a new process has to load and import gradio, etc. (2) slightly slower launch time again due to process creation. The upsides of this approach are (1) letting us scale up the number of independent processes that run your ML model (https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/pull/13998) for faster inference, and (2) also better scaling for the non-ML parts of your Gradio app so the server stays responsive under heavy compute, and this is the groundwork for scaling the web tier separately so your app never gets hugged to death: https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/issues/13617. I.e. we are sacrificing some memory and initial launch time, for better separation of concerns and letting different parts of your app scale up separately which is better for users visiting your app.

**How it works**
- The **gateway** (`gradio/processing/gateway.py`) owns HTTP, the queue, SSE and files, and never imports the app. It rebuilds the UI from the app's config with `Blocks.from_config(..., preserve_ids=True)`, so component and event ids match the app. Every event is forwarded from `route_utils.call_process_api`.
- **The app's process** (`gradio/processing/worker.py`) runs each forwarded event through the same `call_process_api` a normal launch uses. It keeps its own `App` holding the sessions, iterators and `gr.State` caches. Events run concurrently, as they do today.


|demo name|old approach (memory)|this approach (memory)|old approach (latency for api call)|this approach (latency for api call)|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|`hello_world`|233 MB|432 MB|2.4 ms|3.1 ms|
|`calculator`|234 MB|434 MB|3.1 ms|3.3 ms|
|`sepia_filter`|247 MB|447 MB|30.9 ms|32.9 ms|
|`image_mod`|238 MB|438 MB|26.3 ms|26.9 ms|
|`chatinterface_streaming_echo`|234 MB|434 MB|280.5 ms|288.3 ms|
|400 MB model at import|634 MB|834 MB|3.7 ms|7.0 ms|

prs.title: Autoscale the process executor's app processes (memory-aware PoC)
prs.body:
## Description

**Stacked on #14003 (`codex/queue-process-executor`), which targets `7.0-dev`.**

Adds copies of the app's process to the gateway executor of #14003, plus a memory-aware autoscaler that decides when a second copy is worth it. This replaces this PR's earlier per-endpoint worker pool, which #14003 removed.

```python
demo.launch(executor="process", replicas="auto")   # or replicas=2, or GRADIO_PROCESS_REPLICAS
```

- **Replicas** re-run the app script, so each loads its own copy of the models at import; no `resource()` decorator is needed.
- **Sessions stay on the replica that first served them**, since their `gr.State` and generators live there. New sessions go to the least busy replica.
- **`concurrency_limit` applies per replica.** The gateway's queue admits that many events per serving replica.
- **Policy:** `replicas="auto"` runs this PR's existing policy (`poc-3`) in the gateway, where the queue and per-event timings are, with at most two replicas.
  - It starts with one process and records its service times.
  - When events keep waiting for 0.5 s while every process is busy, it checks memory headroom: the first process's observed peak plus 25%, plus a 15% reserve (at least 1 GiB) of system/unified and NVIDIA GPU memory.
  - If that fits, it asks the app's process to start a replica.
  - It keeps the replica only if sustained throughput improves by at least 10% without median latency exceeding 2.5× the baseline.
  - It retires the replica after 60 s idle or when the memory reserve runs low. Real events are never replayed.
- **Status:** `GET /gradio_api/processes` reports the processes, their peak memory and every scaling decision.
- **Kept from before:** `memory.py` (RAM, macOS physical footprint and NVML telemetry, plus the admission check) is unchanged from the earlier version of this PR.

### Results

Each table compares, on the same machine:
- today's thread executor (`concurrency_limit` 1 and 2);
- the #14003 gateway with one process and with two fixed replicas;
- this PR's previous per-endpoint pool (one worker vs auto).

Every run uses the earlier request pattern: 3 warm calls, then two bursts from 12 concurrent clients. The numbers are the second burst, in seconds; lower is better. The ratio in parentheses is against thread / 1 at a time.

**A100 80 GB** (Hugging Face Jobs `a100-large`)

| Workload (requests) | thread, 1 at a time | thread, 2 at a time | gateway, 1 process | gateway, 2 replicas | per-endpoint, 1 worker | per-endpoint, auto |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Pure Python (12) | 14.55 | 14.58 (1.00×) | 14.18 (1.03×) | **7.10 (2.05×)** | 13.96 | **6.95** |
| Kokoro, CUDA (128) | 13.62 | 9.58 (1.42×) | 11.58 (1.18×) | **6.30 (2.16×)** | 11.05 | **6.23** |
| Qwen2.5 7B FP16 (12) | 24.40 | 21.34 (1.14×) | 22.12 (1.10×) | **12.76 (1.91×)** | 21.94 | **12.56** |
| Qwen2.5 32B FP16 (6) | 24.77 | 22.01 (1.13×) | 24.09 (1.03×) | does not fit (63 GB per copy) | — | kept 1 worker earlier |

**Apple M5, 32 GB**

| Workload (requests) | thread, 1 at a time | thread, 2 at a time | gateway, 1 process | gateway, 2 replicas | per-endpoint, 1 worker | per-endpoint, auto |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Pure Python (12) | 2.86 | 2.88 (0.99×) | 2.96 (0.97×) | **1.69 (1.69×)** | 3.01 | **1.46** |
| Kokoro, CPU (64) | 33.17 | **19.31 (1.72×)** | 32.80 (1.01×) | **19.93 (1.66×)** | 33.59 | **18.76** |
| Llama 2 7B Q4, Metal (6) | 13.45 | crashed | 13.69 | 13.60 (no gain) | 13.80 | 13.78 (kept 1) |
| Llama 2 7B Q8, Metal (6) | 22.41 | every request failed | 22.68 | 24.20 (no gain) | 23.82 | 23.36 (kept 1) |

What this shows:
- **On the A100, a second process roughly doubles throughput** for everything whose model fits twice (1.9–2.2×). Two threads help much less (1.0–1.4×), even for CUDA work, because the Python side of each request still contends for the GIL. The cost is a second model copy, for example 30 GB of GPU memory instead of 15 GB for Qwen 7B.
- **Moving the server out of the app's process helps on its own.** With a single process, the gateway is 1.18× faster than thread mode on Kokoro and 1.10× on Qwen 7B.
- **On the M5, a second LLM copy brings nothing**, since the GPU is the bottleneck, so the autoscaler is right to keep one process. For Kokoro on the CPU, two threads already match two processes with half the extra memory.
- **llama.cpp can't serve concurrent requests from threads sharing one model**: it crashed or returned errors. Separate processes are the safe way to run it concurrently.
- **The gateway and the old per-endpoint pool reach the same throughput.** The gateway keeps globals and closures, needs no `resource()`, and loads the model once in single-process mode.

Caveats:
- Each configuration was run once.
- The two-replica columns use a fixed count, which is what `auto` reaches once it keeps a replica. Only Mac pure Python was rerun with the ported autoscaler: 3.21 s with one process vs 1.66 s with auto, after it added, measured and kept a replica.
- Mac and A100 LLM rows use different runtimes, so compare each row only with itself.
- Full tables are in [`demo/autoscale/RESULTS.md`](https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/blob/codex/queue-autoscale-poc/demo/autoscale/RESULTS.md). The raw JSON and logs are in a private dataset.

### Comparison with existing serving libraries

This explores hardware-aware replica scaling for Python functions inside Gradio. It doesn't make an individual inference faster and isn't a vLLM equivalent.
- [Ray Serve](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/serve/autoscaling-guide.html) (`num_replicas="auto"`) and [Modal](https://modal.com/docs/guide/scale) separate replica count, per-replica concurrency and resource allocation, and scale toward demand targets.
- [BentoML](https://docs.bentoml.com/en/latest/reference/bentoml/configurations.html) groups endpoints that share resources (`workers=`).

The new part here is a low-configuration default: measure whether another replica fits on the available hardware, and whether keeping it actually improves throughput.

### Scope and limitations

- At most two replicas, one machine and one GPU.
- Replicas need the app to be run as a script (`python app.py`).
- The server-side state of a session whose replica retires is lost. Browser-held `gr.State` survives, because every process shares the signing secret.
- Memory is observed, not enforced, so unseen inputs can still run out of memory.
- `GET /gradio_api/processes` is not behind the app's `auth=` yet.
- Inherits #14003's process-mode gaps: `cancels=`, `gr.render`, streaming media, custom routes, MCP and reload mode.
